subtopic: Using AI tools inside a team
subtype: Approach: being open with clients about AI use [Action]
passage: Before the contract began, Sarita and Keerthana sat with the school trust's secretary in the Palampur office. Sarita said plainly, 'For the first draft of the newsletter we sometimes use an AI tool, and one of us always checks and edits every line.' Keerthana added that names, fee lists and children's details would never be typed into any such tool. The secretary was quiet, then asked what the tool would be used for, and Sarita showed a sample draft with the edits marked. 'Thank you for telling us,' the secretary said. 'Last year a vendor told us nothing and we found out from a parent.' The secretary asked for the promise to be written into the contract, and Keerthana added a line that same evening.

qa.q: What would never be typed into any such tool?
qa.a: Names, fee lists and children's details would never be typed into any such tool.

qa.q: What did Sarita want the secretary to see by showing the sample draft?
qa.a: Sarita wanted to reassure the secretary that a person checks and edits every line, so the secretary could feel confident the AI use was under control.

qa.q: What could the team do to keep the trust after signing?
qa.a: They could send a short note each quarter saying how AI was used, since repeated honesty keeps the promise alive.

qa.q: What would change for the secretary if the team had said nothing and the truth came out later?
qa.a: The secretary would likely feel misled, as with the vendor last year, and trust would drop, so no promise would have been written into the contract.

grounding: Shows a team telling a client where AI assists in delivery and confirming what data is never shared with tools.

subtopic: Using AI tools inside a team
subtype: Approach: being open with clients about AI use [Action]
passage:
At the kickoff meeting in a Lisbon café, Paulo slid a one-page sheet across the table to Vera, the client's marketing head. 'Before we start, this is how we use AI tools in our work for you.'
Vera raised an eyebrow. 'You're telling me?'
'We'd rather you hear it from us. We use them to draft first versions of social posts and to summarise research. A person rewrites and checks everything. And this column,' he pointed, 'is what never goes into any tool: your customer lists, your sales figures, anything under our confidentiality agreement.'
Vera read it twice. 'My last agency used these tools too. I found out from a mistake in a post.'
'That's why the sheet exists,' Paulo said.
She folded it into her folder. 'Okay. I trust this more than silence.'

qa.q: What never goes into any tool, according to the sheet?
qa.a: Customer lists, sales figures and anything under the confidentiality agreement.

qa.q: How did Vera feel about her last agency?
qa.a: She felt let down, having discovered their AI use only through a mistake in a post.

qa.q: What else could Paulo do to keep Vera's trust?
qa.a: He could update the sheet when tools or uses change and tell Vera before anything new is used on her work.

qa.q: How might Paulo's team be affected by being open?
qa.a: They can work without worrying about being 'found out', and the client relationship starts on firmer ground.

grounding: It shows a team telling a client where AI assists and confirming what data is never shared, building trust through honesty.

subtopic: Using AI tools inside a team
subtype: Approach: being open with clients about AI use [Action]
passage:
In the conference room of the software firm's Kochi office, Thomas put a slide up before the project plan: 'Where we use AI, and where we don't.' Jyoti, the IT head of the cooperative bank they were building for, stopped taking notes.
'We use AI to draft test cases and documentation,' Thomas said. 'A developer reviews every line. We do not use it on your customer data. Nothing from your systems goes into any outside tool, and the tools we use are company-licensed, with training on our inputs switched off.'
Jyoti asked, 'And if that changes?'
'You hear from us first, in writing.'
She was quiet, then smiled. 'Our board asked me to find out whether you use these tools. I didn't expect you to tell me before I asked.'

qa.a: 'Where we use AI, and where we don't.'

qa.q: How does Jyoti seem to feel when Thomas explains?
qa.a: Jyoti seems surprised and reassured, having expected to dig for an answer her board wanted.

qa.q: What else could Thomas's team do to keep this promise?
qa.a: They could send a written note of any change to their AI use before it happens, and revisit it at each quarterly meeting.

qa.q: How might the bank's board see this?
qa.a: The board gets a clear answer early, which builds trust in the firm handling their customers' systems.

grounding: It shows a team telling a client where AI helps in delivery and confirming that client data is not shared with tools, building trust through honesty.
